scope: Read-only source inspection of provider acquisition, client signing, installation proof and account-scoped history. No runtime credentials, private history, deployed configuration, identity tokens or remote requests accessed. Source hashes include actual working-tree bytes; commits alone do not establish cleanliness.

conclusions.android_provider: Credential Manager obtains Google ID token for configured server client ID; RecordsSessionRequest explicitly defaults provider to google. Not evidence of a working Garden sign-in.
conclusions.device_provisioning: UUID v4 plus persisted random 32-byte installation secret; claim sends SHA256 and ios/android platform; later requests send the base64url secret. Server rejects desktop as a claim platform.
conclusions.signing: X-API-Key, Unix-seconds X-Timestamp, HMAC-SHA256(timestamp+exact body) lowercase hex X-Signature. No credential values inspected or copied.
conclusions.owner_boundary: Encrypted Android credentials are keyed to local account identity; publication guards and owner leases reject stale responses during account changes. Signed-in renewal failure must not downgrade requests to anonymous history.
conclusions.desktop: Existing claim endpoint does not offer a desktop platform; a supported desktop identity/device contract is still required.
conclusions.acceptance: Provider acquisition and device claim/Records exchange must be verified in Garden with its own provisioned app identity before private history or reading writes are attached. No source-audit checkbox is treated as end-to-end authentication.
